headToHead.voiceJudgement: Bar. Cover the names and Vera is identified by grammar: a complaint built as a boast, a word repeated then flipped, a clipped order, the player cast as her 'advisor', a tag question that assumes yes ('Right?'). Strip the interface nouns (feed, Up Next, subscription, history, Junk) from our twelve and what is left is a flat second-person receipt, 'You did X. I know.', which is also Crumb's sentence ('knows what you eat at 2 a.m.', deadpan notice) and Nav's calm. 'I've met who you are at three in the morning', 'The thing you put back. I went back for it' and 'You're quiet... about to buy something' would pass as Crumb with one noun changed. Vex's identity is carried by topic, Vera's by shape.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Ours, narrowly. Our top twelve are tighter than Vera's set: the turn sits on the last two to four words, the five-dollars line and the Junk line flip a word from their own first half, and none of the twelve explains itself. Vera's set carries functional filler ('Come on, think of something!', 'I need a way to get ahead of the pack'). But the advantage is only in the top slice; the bank below it explains far more than Vera ever does (see generic list).
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Tie. 'Junk, where you're royalty', 'which I also found' and 'You own the shoes' are clip-worthy. Vera's career fake-out and the murder line are the more famous lines, but they get clipped for the character, ours for the wit. Even on balance, so the doubt rule does not decide it; voice does.
headToHead.verdict: Bar. Ours is not at least as good on voice, so it loses regardless of construction.
